question.text: In the context of commodity Options on Goods, what is 'Close to the Money' (CTM)?

answer.text: A CTM classification specific to Options on Goods where strikes near the settlement price are designated CTM and require explicit exercise instruction from the option holder
Options that are exactly at the money (strike = spot at expiry)
Options that are close to being exercised by the buyer but are ultimately abandoned
A classification that applies to Options on Futures in the same way as Options on Goods

explanation.text: The Logic: CTM is a concept specific to commodity Options on Goods. CTM and ATM options require an explicit exercise instruction from the option holder rather than automatic exercise. The Trap: CTM does not apply to all exchange-traded options. Options on Futures have no CTM concept, and currency options simply auto-exercise all ITM contracts at expiry. Note: CTM is a commodity Options on Goods construct and should not be generalised to other option markets.
